description.p: Point a webcam at your pet and watch from your phone, or watch a pet camera from your computer. Tawny streams video and audio, lets you talk back, and rings a chime to get your pet's attention.
Video and audio go peer to peer over WebRTC, encrypted end to end. There is no account and no sign-up: pairing is a photo of a QR code. Tawny is free, with no ads, no paywall and nothing locked.
Tawny is built with AI: most of its code and documentation was written with Claude, an AI model made by Anthropic, under the maintainer's direction.
Who's here: give yourself a name, then tap the viewer count to see everyone watching the same camera. This computer is listed as a Linux PC rather than a phone.
The web client shared with the Android app no longer relies on a browser call that older web engines lack. Nothing changes in how Tawny Desktop behaves.
The update board now shows after an update even if Tawny was never set up on this computer.
After an update, Tawny shows what changed, with a link to the full changelog and a thank-you to everyone who supports it.
The AppImage starts on systems with a newer NSS than the build machine, instead of crashing at launch, and secure connections work there too. A Monitor using a plain ws:// server can now reach it.

The Monitor shows the safety code for every new phone, not only the first. Pairing with a code-only link at a server that needs a ticket says so, instead of calling the code expired. The safety-code screen is readable in light mode.
Opens on the app's cat, Tawny the owlet and dog. A Viewer whose clock is off no longer calls a fresh pairing code expired.
